item.title: Berlin coalition talks suspended over antisemitism deal concerns
item.description: Germany's Greens and centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) suspended exploratory talks on forming Berlin's next state government with the far-left Left Party on Tuesday to assess whether antisemitism measures agreed to last week still stand.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's Greens and centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) suspended exploratory talks on forming Berlin's next state government with the far-left Left Party on Tuesday to assess whether antisemitism measures [USN:L6N45U0H5 TEXT:"agreed to last week"] still stand. The proposed measures would allow lawmakers accused of antisemitism to be expelled if a panel came to a consensus on the matter. If they disagreed, experts would be called in. The decision comes after the Left admitted lawmaker Vanessa Emde, who has sparked controversy over her stance on Israel, as part of the state of Berlin's new parliamentary group. "We expect the Left to clarify the extent to which they intend to take the agreements we made seriously and implement them," the two parties said in a joint statement after the Left held a constituent meeting. The Left, a hard-left party represented in Berlin by lead candidate Elif Eralp, emerged from the September 20 state election as the largest force, with 25.7% of the votes. Left leader Luigi Pantisano said he was confident that talks could continue, adding that all elected representatives had signed a declaration committing themselves to the fight against antisemitism at their meeting on Tuesday. Tensions over antisemitism and the Israel-Gaza conflict have become a major fault line in German politics, with the SPD and Greens insisting on binding safeguards before entering exploratory coalition talks with the Left.

item.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro reverses course, backs end to six-day workweek
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro on Tuesday said he would back a popular labor reform to reduce the country's workweek, reversing his position in a bid to avoid handing a political win to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, his leftist opponent in Brazil's presidential elections.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro on Tuesday said he would back a popular labor reform to reduce the country's workweek, reversing his position in a bid to avoid handing a political win to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, his leftist opponent in Brazil's presidential elections. The measure, approved by [USN:L1N4230Q1 TEXT:"Brazil's lower house"] in May as a constitutional amendment, would lower working hours in Latin America's largest economy to 40 hours a week from 44, effectively ending a common practice in some sectors, like retail, of requiring employees to work six days a week. Bolsonaro, the son of former right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro, defied pollsters at the start of the month to lead President Lula in the first round of Brazil's election by securing 47% of votes cast. The two men will face each other in a runoff on October 25. Cutting the workweek would mark the biggest overhaul in Brazilian labor rights in decades and a nationwide poll conducted by Quaest in July found nearly 70% of Brazilians support the change. While the senator and his Liberal Party, PL, had long opposed cutting the workweek, arguing the move was designed to boost Lula's reelection prospects, Bolsonaro changed course on Tuesday, just a day before the Senate was expected to vote on the matter. "Most Brazilian workers want to see the end of the six-day workweek, so I'm going to vote in favor of ending it," Bolsonaro told journalists, adding that the government would need to offset impacts on business. Lawmakers aligned with Lula have pushed for a Senate vote before the runoff, hoping to secure approval while the president remains in office. "It seems to me that, following public pressure and street protests, PL decided to vote in favor of ending the six-day workweek," Lula said during an official event on Tuesday. The PL has yet to formally announce a change to its position. "Despite Flavio's lead, the race is still wide open. So it's a smart move by him in avoiding wearing down support on an issue that has broad popular appeal," Leandro Gabiati, director at political consultancy Dominium, said. While business groups say the measure could increase costs and hurt competitiveness, they will not be left too disappointed by Flavio's decision, Gabiati said. "The business community still has many ideological and practical reservations about this government," he said. "It will not feel betrayed by Flavio's change."

FRANKFURT, Oct 13 : The increased use of AI by euro zone companies could curb workers' ability to demand higher wages while heavy investment into the new technology may be materially tightening financing conditions, ECB chief economist Philip Lane said on Tuesday. With inflation now running at nearly twice the ECB's 2 per cent target on expensive energy, policymakers are searching for signs of second-round price effects, but have so far concluded there are none, especially in wage growth. While AI has not changed employment trends, hiring plans are muted and this limits workers' ability to demand compensation for high inflation, Lane said, offering a potential explanation for why wage growth is slowing, despite high inflation. "The potential for AI to replace some types of workers may also weaken the bargaining power of workers, moderating wage growth and reducing the labour share in total income," Lane said in a speech in Dublin.

While Lane did not directly discuss current monetary policy, he said that companies around the globe are borrowing so heavily to fund AI that this is pushing up borrowing costs for everyone and tightening financing conditions by a rate that is now relevant for ECB policy. "The spillover to the euro area bond market means that the increase in long-term interest rates constitutes a material tightening of financial conditions for the euro area," Lane said. "This is a relevant factor for the ECB in determining the appropriate monetary policy stance." The comments are significant since the ECB has been raising interest rates to prevent inflation from getting embedded and tighter overall financing conditions could mean the ECB may need to do less to tame price growth, some economists say. AI could also have a relevant impact for the economy over the longer term, raising potential output and trend growth, which would increase the economy's potential 'speed limit,' Lane said. "For Europe, the potential for AI to offset the economic impact of the projected trend decline in the working-age population is especially valuable," he said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 台湾、欧州の中国依存リスク警告 外交部長「自由や主権の脅威に」
item.description: [ワルシャワ １３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワルシャワ　１３日　ロイター] - 台湾の林佳龍外交部長（外相）は１３日、訪問先のポーランドで演説し、欧州連合（ＥＵ）が中国によるサプライチェーン（供給網）を通じた支配にさらされないよう促した。「中国の権威主義的イデオロギーは、欧州の民主主義とは相いれない。中国への依存は単なる経済的リスクにとどまらず、欧州の自由や主権にとって脅威となる」と警告した。

１５日に開幕するＥＵ首脳会議では、中国への対応も協議される。ＥＵは対中貿易赤字の縮小のほか、重点分野での中国依存の軽減を目指している。

林氏はワルシャワ・セキュリティー・フォーラムで「台湾と欧州は、民主主義や自由、人権、法の支配という重要な価値観を共有している」と述べ、台湾との貿易拡大が欧州にとっても有益だと主張した。

台湾は、２０２２年のロシアによるウクライナ侵攻以降、欧州との関係強化を目指している。ポーランドは台湾との正式な外交関係はないものの、林氏は外交部長に就任して以降、数回にわたり欧州を訪問している。一方、中国は、台湾当局者が海外を訪問することに非難を繰り返している。

item.title: トルコ大統領、サウジ支持継続を表明 フーシ派攻撃受け
item.description: [アンカラ １３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[アンカラ １３日 ロイター] - トルコのエルドアン大統領は１３日、サウジアラビアのムハンマド皇太子と電話会談を行い、 イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派による攻撃が続く中、引き続きサウジアラビアを支持していく方針を伝えた。

トルコ大統領府によると、エルドアン氏はフーシ派による攻撃を強く非難した上で、ムハンマド皇太子に対し、「この試練は乗り越えられると信じている」と述べた。

北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）に加盟するトルコ、核保有国のパキスタン、サウジの３カ国は８月にメッカ共同防衛協定に署名。同協定は集団的抑止力の強化を目的としており、署名国のいずれか１カ国に対する攻撃は３カ国全てに対する攻撃と見なすと定めている。

item.title: 来年は米追加利上げ不要、インフレ鈍化見込む─ＮＹ連銀総裁＝報道
item.description: [１３日 ロイター] - 米ニューヨーク連銀のウィリアムズ総裁は、年内にあと１回の利上げが適切との見方を依然として維持...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
来年は米追加利上げ不要、インフレ鈍化見込む─ＮＹ連銀総裁＝報道 3:32 配信

米ニューヨーク連銀のウィリアムズ総裁。2025年9月撮影。REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

[１３日　ロイター] - 米ニューヨーク連銀のウィリアムズ総裁は、年内にあと１回の利上げが適切との見方を依然として維持しているものの、現時点で連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が２０２７年に再び利上げする必要があるとは考えていないと述べた。ブルームバーグ・ニュースが１３日に伝えた。

ウィリアムズ総裁はインタビューで、「あと１回の利上げが適切との私の見方は変わっていない」と述べ、年内の追加利上げを支持する姿勢を示した。２７年については「現時点でこれ以上の対応が必要と考える理由はない」と言及。データ次第で見通しが変わる可能性に含みを残し、「来年については様子を見守る必要がある。まだ１０月中旬だ。米経済はさまざまな要因の影響を受けており、われわれはデータを注視し続けなければならない」と語った。

また同総裁は、インフレ率は時間をかけてＦＲＢの目標である２％に向かって鈍化していくと予想していると述べた。ただ、短期的なインフレ圧力は中東での戦争に伴うエネルギー価格の高騰の影響を受けていると指摘。ハイテク部門への投資もインフレ押し上げ要因になっているとの見方を示した。

「依然としてディスインフレの力が働いていると信じている」とした上で、「来年はインフレがかなり鈍化し、通年でみれば、全体のインフレ率は目標の２％近辺になるとみている。これは私が言及した要因、すなわち関税の影響が完全に過去のものとなることを反映している」と語った。

さらに、「来年以降はエネルギー価格がインフレを押し上げることはないと引き続き考えている」とした上で、米国経済は全体として過熱している状況ではないと述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：米長期金利5％接近で株式市場に警戒感、決算後はマクロ要因に注目 焦点：ベセント氏発言で強まる日銀9月利上げ観測、米国の影響力拡大に懸念も アングル：米国債「ツイスト・スティープ化」、ＦＲＢの信認巡る懸念反映か アングル：インフレで揺らぐ債券のヘッジ機能、米投資家は実物資産に移行 最終更新: 10/14(水) 4:56 ロイター

item.title: トランプ氏、フーシ派が米中間選挙前に原油価格つり上げと非難
item.description:
Jacob Bogage
[ワシントン １３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jacob Bogage

[ワシントン １３日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１３日、米国とイランの戦争を受けて中東地域の紛争が拡大する中、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派が１１月の米中間選挙を前に意図的に原油価格をつり上げようとしていると非難した。また、サウジアラビアに対するフーシ派の攻撃を「決して忘れない」と警告した。

トランプ氏は自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で、「フーシ派は非常に悪い振る舞いをしている」と非難。昨年の米国によるイエメン空爆後、比較的平穏な時期が続いていたものの、同派はイランの指示を受けて攻撃を再開したと主張した。

さらに、自身の警告は１１月３日の中間選挙後も続くとの考えを明確にし、「選挙後も私はそこにいるし、決して忘れない！」と述べた。

トランプ氏はこれに先立ち記者団に対し、サウジの国益を守るため、トルコのエルドアン大統領に介入を要請する「可能性がある」とし、「エルドアン大統領は私の要請に応じてくれると思う」と述べていた。

フーシ派はここ数日で、サウジアラビアの首都リヤドにあるキング・ハーリド国際空港を攻撃し、１３人が死亡、３００人以上が負傷したほか、リヤド上空の空域が閉鎖された。

item.title: Fed's Williams sees no need for rate hike in 2027, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams has reaffirmed his view that the US central bank may need to raise interest rates once more this year in its bid to lower inflation.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams has reaffirmed his view that the US central bank may need to raise interest rates once more this year in its bid to lower inflation. "I haven't changed my view that it may be appropriate to have one more rate hike" in 2026, Williams told Bloomberg News in an interview published on Tuesday. And when it comes to 2027, "I don't think at this time I have any reason to believe that we would need to do more," Williams said, though he left the door open for data to change that outlook. "We'll have to see" what happens next year, Williams said, adding that "it's still mid-October. This economy is being affected by lots of different influences, and we just have to keep watching the data." The Fed raised its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"3.75%-4.00% range"] last month. Speaking less than two weeks after that rate hike, Williams, who also serves as vice chair of the central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, [USN:L6N45L17G TEXT:"reshaped market expectations"] about the policy outlook when he said there was no urgency to follow up the move with another rate increase. Williams, speaking at an event in Buffalo on September 29, said the Fed probably needed to deliver only one more hike in 2026. Those remarks last month caused investors to price out the prospect of a hike at the Fed's October 27-28 meeting. Other central bank officials have echoed that lack of urgency to follow the September hike with more tightening. Williams' comments about the outlook were notable given that Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has said little publicly about the policy outlook. In the Bloomberg interview, Williams said he expects inflation to ease toward the Fed's 2% target over time, but added that near-term price pressures were being affected by high energy prices tied to the war in the Middle East. He also said investment tied to the tech sector is pushing up inflation. "I still believe there's disinflationary forces at play," Williams told Bloomberg. "My forecast for inflation for next year is inflation to come down quite a bit — overall inflation to be near our 2% target for the year as a whole next year, and that's reflecting some of these factors I mentioned, that the tariffs will be totally in the rearview mirror," he said. "I still believe that energy prices will not be adding to inflation next year or after that," Williams said. "My view is this is not an economy that is overheating overall," he added. "This is not an economy where it's adding inflationary pressures beyond these particular shocks that we're experiencing."

item.title: Grok cases highlight risks for AI companies under Illinois privacy law
item.description: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI has been hit with two proposed class actions alleging its Grok platform violates a stringent Illinois privacy law through its manipulation of facial images, marking the latest lawsuits against AI companies over their collection and use of biometric data.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI has been hit with two proposed class actions alleging its Grok platform violates a stringent Illinois privacy law through its manipulation of facial images, marking the latest lawsuits against AI companies over their collection and use of biometric data. The cases against SpaceXAI were filed in the federal court in Chicago, one of which was filed on Monday. They both allege that the company, formerly known as xAI, illegally collected and used an individual’s biometric information from an uploaded "selfie" photo without written notice. SpaceXAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Tuesday. The lawsuits are part of a growing wave of litigation targeting how AI companies are using personal information such as facial scans and voiceprints to build and operate their platforms. Alphabet's Google and notetaking and organizing app Otter.ai are among defendants also facing class action claims under the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act. The Illinois law restricts the collection and use of personal information such as retinal scans and fingerprints, and for many years has posed compliance hurdles and litigation headaches for companies. In 2020, Facebook said it would pay $650 million to resolve class action allegations that it violated the Illinois law. Freight rail giant BNSF in 2024 [USN:L2N3FC0C0 TEXT:"agreed"] to pay $75 million to resolve a class action under BIPA. Plaintiffs' law firms are increasingly bringing lawsuits alleging BIPA violations related to AI. Defense firm Paul Hastings had warned in an advisory in April that “a new wave of biometrics litigation has arrived” targeting AI companies. In one of the cases, a group of journalists [USN:L6N41P10X TEXT:"sued"] Alphabet’s Google in May in a proposed class action alleging it illegally used recordings of their voices to train AI models. Google has denied the claims and asked a court to dismiss them, saying the plaintiffs failed to allege that Google obtained any biometric voice identifier linked to a specific individual. Otter.ai is facing other cases as well. Those lawsuits, consolidated in federal court in California, contend the company is violating BIPA by collecting and creating voiceprints associated with recorded speakers. Otter has denied the allegations and asked a judge to dismiss the lawsuits. The lawsuits against SpaceXAI allege Grok violates the Illinois law when it performs without prior consent "face-specific analysis or identity-preserving image manipulation" after a user uploads a photograph. BIPA applies even when a user uploads their own photo, the lawsuits say. “As businesses worldwide compete to develop ever more advanced artificial intelligence and facial-analysis technology, the race for data imperils the privacy of individuals everywhere,” the complaint filed last week said. Read more: [USN:L6N44F19B TEXT:"Lawyers square off in fight over voice data used to train AI"] [USN:L6N41P10X TEXT:"Journalists sue Google for allegedly using their voices in AI training"] [USN:L2N3FC0C0 TEXT:"BNSF Railway to pay $75 mln to resolve biometric privacy class-action"]

item.title: De la Espriella pierde imagen positiva y Sheinbaum se consolida entre presidentes mejor valorados de América Latina
item.description: Keiko Fujimori, presidenta de Perú, presenta la mayor caída del ranking, con una disminución de −6,1 puntos porcentuales respecto de la medición del mes pasado.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, se ubicó como la mandataria con mayor favorabilidad de América Latina en octubre, mientras que el colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella fue el único que registró una caída en su respaldo entre los seis mejor evaluados. Ver más: Los países que más crecerían en Latinoamérica en 2026 y 2027, tras nuevo ajuste del Banco Mundial Claudia Sheinbaum encabeza el listado de los presidentes con mayor favorabilidad en América Latina con el 69,3% de imagen positiva, según el informe de CB Global Data. Un 33,3% de los encuestados tiene una imagen muy positiva de la presidenta mexicana, mientras que para el 36% es buena. A comienzos de octubre, Sheinbaum afirmó que su principal aliado es “el pueblo” mexicano, al ser consultada sobre la posible pérdida de aliados regionales tras la primera vuelta electoral en Brasil que resultó con la victoria del ultraderechista Flávio Bolsonaro. “Mientras estemos cerca del pueblo, representando al pueblo, y gobernando por el pueblo y para el pueblo, no va a haber problema, ninguno, en México, ese es nuestro gran aliado”, declaró. “Una vez que termine todo el proceso (en Brasil), podremos dar opinión”, declaró. Ver más: Sheinbaum minimiza pérdida de aliados en Latinoamérica tras derrota de Lula en Brasil A Sheinbaum le siguen en favorabilidad el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, con el 68,3%, y el de República Dominicana, Luis Abinader, con el 51,9% de aprobación. En ambos casos se registró una mejora frente a los indicadores de respaldo registrados en septiembre. También mejoró la favorabilidad de la presidenta de Costa Rica, Laura Fernández, cuya imagen positiva pasó del 49,7% de septiembre al 51% en octubre En cambio, cayó la imagen positiva del mandatario colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella, que recién completó dos meses de gobierno. La imagen positiva de De la Espriella cayó del 53,6% en septiembre al 49,7% en octubre. Organizaciones sindicales, indígenas y sociales alistan una jornada de protestas el próximo miércoles en Colombia, que pondrá a prueba el respaldo al Gobierno de Abelardo de la Espriella. Las movilizaciones responden al rechazo de un sector de la población a las medidas del Gobierno de Abelardo de la Espriella y a la preocupación por posibles restricciones al derecho a la protesta social. El estudio de CB Global Data abarcó a población mayor de 18 años en 18 países de América Latina, con muestras de entre 1.959 y 3.911 casos por país. La encuesta tiene un margen de error entre +/-1,6% y 2,2%, así como un nivel de confianza del 95%. El trabajo de campo fue realizado del 5 al 8 de octubre de 2026. Ver más: Colombia le ofrece a EE.UU. sus minerales críticos: qué dicen los memorandos y qué riesgos existen Keiko Fujimori, presidenta de Perú, está entre los mandatarios latinoamericanos con una aprobación “regular”, según la encuesta de CB Global Data. Fujimori, que tomó el mando presidencial ante el Congreso de Perú el pasado 28 de julio, tiene un respaldo del 46,3% frente a un 50,8% de desaprobación. La presidenta de Perú presenta la mayor caída del ranking, con una disminución de −6,1 puntos porcentuales respecto de la medición del mes pasado. Le sigue en la octava posición el presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, con una favorabilidad de 45,3% y una desaprobación 50,5%. La aprobación de Lula cayó en relación con el 48,5% de septiembre, en medio de la carrera electoral en ese país. Según una encuesta de AtlasIntel para Bloomberg News, el senador Flávio Bolsonaro obtendría el 53% de los votos válidos frente al 47% del presidente Lula da Silva en la segunda vuelta del 25 de octubre, En la novena posición se ubica Nasry Asfura, presidente de Honduras, quien tiene un 44,1% de apoyo y un 53,9% de rechazo. Sin embargo, dentro de los mandatarios clasificados con una aprobación “regular”, Asfura es el único que muestra una tendencia al alza respecto a su dato previo del 43,2%. El décimo lugar lo ocupa el presidente de Paraguay, Santiago Peña, con una aprobación del 42,9% y un 52,7% de desaprobación. Ya en el undécimo puesto se encuentra el mandatario de Bolivia, Rodrigo Paz, con un 41,1% de imagen positiva y un 53,5% negativa. Y en el duodécimo lugar figura el presidente de Chile, José Antonio Kast, que tiene un 38,8% de aprobación frente a un 56,8% de desaprobación. Entre los mandatarios peor evaluados figura en el puesto 13 José Raúl Mulino, presidente de Panamá, con un 36,5% de aprobación y un 58,9% de desaprobación. A pesar de ello, José Raúl Mulino es el presidente que registra la mayor recuperación, con una subida de +4,4 puntos porcentuales frente a la encuesta de septiembre. Le sigue el mandatario de Argentina, Javier Milei, con un 36,1% de aprobación y un 59% de desaprobación. La imagen de Milei registró un leve aumento, desde el 35,5% previo. En el puesto 15 se encuentra Daniel Ortega, de Nicaragua, con un 35,7% de aprobación y un 60,3% de desaprobación. En el caso de Ortega también hubo un aumento en su tasa de favorabilidad, ya que en septiembre esta estaba en el 33,9%. En la posición 16 figura Yamandú Orsi, de Uruguay, con un 35,2% de aprobación y un 62,1% de desaprobación. El puesto 17 lo ocupa Delcy Rodríguez, presidenta interina de Venezuela, con un 32,3% de aprobación y un 60,9% de desaprobación. Sin embargo, su favorabilidad aumentó frente al 28,8% anterior. Bernardo Arévalo, mandatario de Guatemala, cierra el ranking en la posición 18, con un 31% de aprobación y un 63,1% de desaprobación. Ver más: Bernardo Arévalo rinde cuentas tras dos años de gobierno en Guatemala

item.title: India-US trade talks heading in right direction, Jaishankar says as both sides work to finalise a deal
item.description: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar says India-US trade negotiations are moving in the right direction, with a deal being worked out. However, changing US tariff policies and unresolved trade issues continue to complicate the agreement’s finalisation.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Bhattacharya
item.content:encoded: India’s trade negotiations with the United States are moving in the right direction, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Tuesday, 13 October, signalling continued efforts to finalise an agreement despite differences over tariffs and market access.India-US trade talks moving in right direction, Jaishankar saysJaishankar’s remarks offer a positive indication from New Delhi as the two countries attempt to conclude a trade pact that has taken longer than initially anticipated. A deal is still being worked out, however, and his comments do not mean that a final agreement has been signed.The minister’s assessment comes amid uncertainty over Washington’s changing tariff policies and their implications for Indian exporters. The negotiations have become an important part of the broader India-US relationship, with both sides seeking to strengthen commercial ties while protecting their domestic economic interests.According to financial news service Newsquawk, Jaishankar said the talks were heading in the right direction and that a deal was being ironed out. Why the trade agreement has taken longer India and the US announced a framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement in February 2026. Subsequent changes to American tariff policy, however, complicated the process and prompted further discussions. In September, Jaishankar acknowledged that the negotiations had been more complex than expected, pointing to differences between the two economies and the need to protect sensitive domestic sectors. India has a large base of small manufacturers, agricultural producers and businesses whose interests could be affected by changes in import duties and market access. New Delhi has therefore sought to ensure that any agreement offers Indian exporters competitive terms without exposing vulnerable sectors to excessive pressure. At an event hosted by the Asia Society in New York, Jaishankar said the two sides had reached a stage where there was “more or less an understanding on the trade agreement”. He also cautioned that the remaining issues required careful consideration. US tariff uncertainty remains a sticking point One of the key complications is the evolving American tariff framework, including the ongoing Section 301 process. The provision allows the United States to investigate foreign trade practices it considers unfair and potentially impose additional duties.Jaishankar has questioned when India should conclude an agreement while aspects of the US tariff regime remain unsettled. The uncertainty matters because Indian exporters need clarity on the duties their products will face in the American market.India is also seeking tariff terms that allow its businesses to compete effectively with exporters from other countries.Reuters reported on 6 October that the negotiations had encountered fresh obstacles, with officials describing limited progress towards an imminent deal.Deal could help stabilise bilateral tiesTrade has become a significant source of friction between New Delhi and Washington, alongside disagreements on other diplomatic and economic issues.Jaishankar has previously said that concluding the agreement could help put bilateral relations on a better footing. For businesses, a settled framework could provide greater certainty on tariffs, market access and investment. For now, his latest remarks suggest that negotiations remain active, but important questions are unresolved. The next step will be to translate the stated progress into an agreement acceptable to both governments.Until the terms are formally concluded, Indian exporters and US businesses will have to contend with uncertainty over the future trading arrangements between the two countries.

item.title: Lawmakers ask FAA to pause use of new AI tool in DC-area flight management
item.description: More than two dozen lawmakers asked the Federal Aviation Administration to pause the use of a new AI tool in the Washington area to assist air traffic controllers, citing safety concerns.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: More than two dozen lawmakers asked the Federal Aviation Administration to pause the use of a new AI tool in the Washington area to assist air traffic controllers, citing safety concerns. The lawmakers, including Democratic Representatives April Delaney, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Don Beyer, said in a letter they were concerned with the FAA pilot project "as we have not seen any safety evaluation and testing reports, nor have we been made aware of any efforts to train aviation safety personnel on how best to use the tool." The letter seeks an answer by Oct. 19. "Air traffic control leaves zero margin for error," Ocasio-Cortez said Tuesday, calling for the pause. The FAA last month began using a new software-based AI tool system that uses predictive analytics to improve how flights are managed. "We are deeply concerned about the integration of any AI-enabled system into air traffic control systems, where decisions are literally a matter of life or death," said the letter that was also signed by Senator Chris Van Hollen and Representatives Jamie Raskin, Raja Krishnamoorthi and Kweisi Mfume. The FAA in June awarded an $875 million, 12-year contract to Air Space Intelligence for a system dubbed Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories or SMART, which uses data to analyze airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur. The FAA is initially using the AI tool in the airspace around Washington, D.C. and plans to gradually expand it to other parts of the country. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Tuesday called the tool essentially "dumb AI" and emphasized controllers remain in charge -- not the software. "Air traffic controllers will always control the airspace. This is just giving additional tools for controllers to better manage" weather and other issues," Duffy said on Fox Business' "Big Money in the Morning." The system uses over 200 data streams, creates data visualizations, and produces scheduling recommendations for operations experts to consider passing along but does not involve active management of planes in the sky, USDOT said. "It's going to be transformational," FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told Reuters earlier. "We'll make much better decisions if we have better decision-making tools." The plan is to initially use it to more effectively reschedule flights that were canceled due to bad weather with plans to expand to other tasks such as strategically coordinating schedules and trajectories before aircraft depart.

item.content:encoded: A dozen US senators, including six Republicans, called on President Donald Trump on Tuesday to rescind his diesel deal with Russia , days before his administration must decide whether to formally impose new sanctions on Moscow over its war in Ukraine. The lawmakers' letter to Trump said the agreement provides Russian President Vladimir Putin's government with more fuel to finance its war , and will not benefit Americans, adding to a torrent of congressional criticism since Trump announced the deal on Friday. The resistance marks a shift from what had been Republicans' near-unanimous support for Trump's foreign policy decisions, weeks before November 3 midterm elections that will determine whether the party retains control of Congress. In his post, Trump said he was lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports, and that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons (2.25 million barrels) of diesel to US and global markets. Although Trump said he wanted to reduce prices, the amount he referenced is less than a day's supply for the US transport sector alone, according to US Energy Information Administration data, which shows daily use of around 2.94 million barrels per day. "Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin's murderous, illegal war," the lawmakers said in their letter. "This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded," they said. The senators' letter, dated Tuesday, was signed by Republicans Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Susan Collins of Maine, Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and John Cornyn of Texas, as well as six Democrats. GRAHAM SANCTIONS BILL DEADLINE LOOMS Under [USN:L1N4570ZO TEXT:"a law"] Trump signed last month, he faces an October 18 deadline to impose sweeping new sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy over the Ukraine war, or waive them because he has determined that doing so is in the national interest. The letter urged Trump to execute the sanctions authorities included in the new law, called the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026", in honor of the late senator, a Russia hawk and close Trump ally who died in July. The administration has not yet told lawmakers whether it would impose the sanctions or issue a waiver. Collins, Murkowski and Tillis had joined Democrats in a [USN:O8N43T024 TEXT:"joint statement"] on Sunday calling on Trump to "reverse course" on [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"the deal"], saying it runs counter to US law barring imports of energy until Russia ends its aggression against Ukraine. Earlier on Tuesday, the Republican president [USN:S0N435010 TEXT:"was asked"] whether anyone had told him Russia could use proceeds of the diesel deal to purchase more bombs. "No, nobody told me anything," Trump responded, adding the deal benefited not just the US but the world. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak [USN:S8N45E0D7 TEXT:"said on Monday"] that Russia will be able to return diesel exports to levels above those Trump had outlined under the deal. The Democratic senators who signed the letter were Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Durbin of Illinois, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Jack Reed of Rhode Island and Chris Coons of Connecticut.

item.title: CVS settles US Justice Department case over opioid prescriptions for $315 million
item.description: CVS Health has agreed to pay $315 million to resolve allegations that the pharmacy chain operator unlawfully filled medically unnecessary prescriptions for addictive opioid painkillers, the US Justice Department said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: CVS Health (CVS.N) has agreed to pay $315 million to resolve allegations that the pharmacy chain operator unlawfully filled medically unnecessary prescriptions for addictive opioid painkillers, the US Justice Department said on Tuesday. The settlement resolves a case the department [USN:L1N3NJ131 TEXT:"announced in 2024"] that sought to hold CVS responsible for its role in dispensing massive quantities of dangerous drugs like opioids that were at the heart of a nationwide addiction epidemic. The lawsuit alleged that CVS since 2013 had illegally filled prescriptions for opioids and other narcotics in violation of the federal Controlled Substances Act and then sought payment from federal healthcare programs like Medicare in violation of the False Claims Act. As part of the settlement, CVS entered into an agreement with the Drug Enforcement Administration under which the chain would establish processes to monitor and receive reports of potentially illegal dispensing in its pharmacies and evaluate doctors suspected of illegally prescribing opioids. “Today's settlement is a significant milestone in the Justice Department's efforts to combat the opioid epidemic by cracking down on pharmacies who unlawfully fulfill prescriptions for controlled substances," Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward said in a statement. CVS said in a statement that it disagreed with the Justice Department's allegations and was not admitting wrongdoing. "Our more than 27,000 CVS pharmacists do their part to help keep America healthy and are highly trained in the safe and appropriate use of all medications," CVS said. The Justice Department [USN:L6N44P0PK TEXT:"settled"] a similar case in August against rival pharmacy chain operator Walmart, which agreed to pay $50 million to resolve a 2020 lawsuit alleging it unlawfully dispensed opioid prescriptions. CVS agreed to pay close to $5 billion in 2022 to settle thousands of similar claims by state, local and Native American tribal governments, which had pursued a series of related cases against other drug companies and pharmacy chains accused of fueling an opioid addiction epidemic in the US . The Justice Department's lawsuit, which was filed in federal court in Rhode Island, began as a whistleblower complaint brought by a former CVS employee. The lawsuit alleged that the company dispensed prescriptions for dangerous and excessive amounts of opioids and other drugs and filled prescriptions from doctors running so-called pill mills that prescribed large amounts of addictive opioids that lacked any legitimate medical purpose. The lawsuit noted that CVS had been among the top dispensers of opioids in the nation, selling over 12 billion doses of the drugs from 2015 to 2020.

item.title: Police clash with Imran Khan supporters in northwestern Pakistan
item.description: Police fired tear gas and live rounds at supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan in northwestern Pakistan on Tuesday as clashes erupted over the suspension of his party's provincial government, party officials said, an account the provincial administration rejected.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Police fired tear gas and live rounds at supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan in northwestern Pakistan on Tuesday as clashes erupted over the suspension of his party's provincial government, party officials said, an account the provincial administration rejected. The federal government imposed a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Sunday and placed it under direct control, citing a surge in militant violence. Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party said that was a pretext for a political takeover. Samar Haroon Bilour, who handles information for the provincial administration, said in a written response to Reuters that allegations of live firing by police were “baseless and frivolous” and were spread by anonymous social media accounts using AI-generated footage. She said police had responded to rioting and vandalism in a calibrated way, and that about 50 people had been arrested and four cases registered under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Khan’s aide and PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari shared videos on X that he linked to the violence in Bara Bazaar, calling the emergency and governor’s rule a coup and warning it could spread. Reuters could not independently verify the footage or the competing accounts of the shooting. Five people were injured in the clashes that occurred in the province, party officials said, the most serious of them in Bara, about 15 km (9 miles) from the provincial capital Peshawar. PTI information secretary Ikram Khatana said unidentified people set fire to the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) center in Bara and stormed nearby offices. Bilour said responsibility for the NADRA incident would be established through the investigation, including video footage and witness statements. The sacking of PTI's only provincial government is the latest blow against Khan, who has been in prison since 2023. He has been accused of inciting riots targeting military sites as well as corruption and other charges. His wife, three sisters and scores of activists are also under detention. Khan denies the allegations and says they are politically motivated.

item.title: Saudi Arabia plans hybrid format for marquee FII conference after attacks, sources say
item.description: Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship investment conference a hybrid event, giving executives the option to tune in remotely, after deadly weekend attacks on Riyadh airport prompted a rethink of travel to the kingdom, said two people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship investment conference a hybrid event, giving executives the option to tune in remotely, after deadly [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"weekend attacks on Riyadh airport"] prompted a rethink of travel to the kingdom, said two people familiar with the matter. Some participants were still expected to fly in and could land at airstrips outside Riyadh, or even in neighbouring Gulf states, and then drive to the capital to attend the Future Investment Initiative scheduled for later this month, said one of the people. The Saudi government media office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Earlier this month organisers [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"said the event would go ahead"] despite missile attacks in the kingdom. Asked for comment, an FII media representative pointed Reuters to a statement from the CEO and chairman of the FII Institute sent before Saturday's attacks. "As we prepare to welcome thousands of delegates to Riyadh for the exceptional 10th edition of the Future Investment Initiative, their safety and well-being remain our highest priority," said CEO Maha Al Saud and Richard Attias, chairman of the executive committee. 'DAVOS IN THE DESERT' Major oil bosses [USN:L6N45Y0GT TEXT:"dropped out of an international conference"] on Monday and a hybrid model would allow for more participants to take part. The move shows how Saudi Arabia is trying to maintain its push to attract global investment despite an [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"escalating war with the Houthis"] that has challenged its efforts to turn Riyadh into a hub for global events. The kingdom has used the FII to showcase its plans to diversify its economy from oil and attract foreign investments. The typical attendance of a large number of world leaders, corporate chieftains and financiers has led the event to be nicknamed "Davos in the desert," in a nod to the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Switzerland. Global financial titans, including Goldman Sachs (GS.N) CEO and Chairman David Solomon, Standard Chartered (STAN.L) CEO Bill Winters and Citi's CEO Jane Fraser, were scheduled to participate as speakers at the event, according to a draft programme on the FII website dated October 6. Citi (C.N) and Goldman Sachs declined to comment on the executives' attendance, while Standard Chartered had no immediate comment. The FII event, in its 10th edition, is due to be held at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Centre, on the western edge of Riyadh.

item.title: Delaware jury awards Qualcomm $2 in damages, finds Arm breached license agreement
item.description: Chip technology supplier Arm Holdings breached a licensing agreement with Qualcomm and intentionally interfered with the chipmaker's business relationship with Meta Platforms , a Delaware jury found on Tuesday, but awarded nominal damages of just $2.
item.dc:creator: Tom Hals
item.content:encoded: Chip technology supplier Arm Holdings (O9Ty.F) breached a licensing agreement with Qualcomm (QCOM.O) and intentionally interfered with the chipmaker's business relationship with Meta Platforms (META.O) , a Delaware jury found on Tuesday, but awarded nominal damages of just $2. The verdict followed a five-day trial last week, the second in two years between the companies, that highlighted the deterioration of their business relationship after SoftBank Group (9984.T) acquired control of Arm in 2016 and Arm shifted from licensing the technology needed to make chips to selling chips of its own. Shares of Arm were down 1% following the verdict, while shares of Qualcomm rose 1%, although its stock was down slightly from gains of around 2.4% before the verdict. Both companies welcomed aspects of the verdict, which leaves some key issues unresolved. "We are gratified that the jury found Arm breached its long-standing Architectural License Agreement (ALA) with Qualcomm, failed to honor its commitments, and intentionally acted to disrupt Qualcomm's businesses," Qualcomm said in a statement. Arm said that "despite Qualcomm’s pursuit of this case in an attempt to deprive Arm of billions of dollars under our license agreements, the jury’s verdict confirms that Arm operated in good faith under its technology license agreement and its award of only two dollars confirms the merit of Arm’s arguments in the case." The jury found Arm breached its obligation to provide software patches and tools for its designs. The jury found for Arm on five other breach allegations. The jury also found that Arm intentionally and negligently interfered with Qualcomm's relations with Meta. Qualcomm claimed it had been on the cusp of a deal with Meta in 2024 when Arm allegedly leaked to Bloomberg News that Qualcomm had breached a licensing agreement, delaying the Meta agreement. While the jury awarded a nominal $1 for each of those claims, the findings also keep open Qualcomm's claims ahead of the lawsuit's next phase, in which US District Judge Maryellen Noreika must resolve several disputes. The breach finding leaves open the possibility that Noreika could rule that as a result, Qualcomm can stop paying royalties to Arm for five years, potentially worth billions of dollars. Arm has argued the five-year royalty penalty, which is contained in a clause in the licensing agreement, is unenforceable. The business interference finding by the jury could be used by Qualcomm to support its narrative that Arm refused to negotiate in good faith for Arm's next version of its technology, which the judge also must resolve. The losing side in those decisions would likely appeal.

item.title: UK regulator FCA to publish whistleblower review in early 2027
item.description: Britain's markets regulator plans to publish a report early next year into whether it could have done more in its interactions with a whistleblower, the Financial Conduct Authority said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's markets regulator plans to publish a report early next year into whether it could have done more in its interactions with a whistleblower, the Financial Conduct Authority said on Tuesday. • FCA Chief Executive Nikhil Rathi told lawmakers the death of Simon Andriesz last month was "terribly sad" and that it was important for the regulator to reflect on how it communicated and engaged with whistleblowers. • The FCA had been in contact with Andriesz over many years and his death sparked questions by lawmakers about whether it took his allegations sufficiently seriously. • Andriesz died by suicide last month. John Robertson, one of his representatives, has said he had been recognised as a whistleblower in the US but did not feel he received the same level of engagement from British authorities. • The cross-party Treasury Committee asked whether the FCA had considered asking an external expert to review the case. Rathi said that Lea Paterson, who joined the FCA's board this month, would launch the review as an independent non-executive. • Paterson is expected to examine whether there were things the FCA could have done better and help the organisation learn for the future. • The FCA has said the number of whistleblowing reports rose by 22% last year. Around 42% led to direct action and another 53% informed its wider work and supported harm prevention.

item.title: US chip stocks slide as China’s CXMT advances; AI spending fears rattle investors
item.description: Shares in US chip manufacturers tumbled, primarily influenced by memory and data storage firms, following competitive moves from China's CXMT. The sector faced significant pressure, stemming from concerns over escalating rivalry and demands for AI investments. Key players like Micron Technology, Seagate Technology, SanDisk, and Western Digital saw notable declines in their stock prices.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: US chip stocks fell on Tuesday, led by memory-chip and data-storage companies, after reports of a technological advance by China’s CXMT raised concerns about intensifying competition. Questions about heavy artificial-intelligence spending added to pressure on a sector that has rallied sharply this year, Reuters reported.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 1.5%, extending its decline to a fifth consecutive session and touching its lowest level in about four weeks.Micron Technology fell 4.5% to its lowest level since September 16, marking its fourth straight daily decline. Data-storage companies also suffered steep losses, with SanDisk down 4.3%, Seagate Technology falling 5.9% and Western Digital sliding 5.8%.According to the Reuters report, Chinese memory-chip maker CXMT has made “key progress” on a new cell architecture designed to increase memory density. South Korea’s Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are working on similar technology.Samsung shares tumbled more than 7% in South Korea, while SK Hynix dropped over 10%.Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth, described the selloff as a rush to lock in profits as investors reassess the threat of greater competition.Concerns about AI investment also weighed on the sector after Broadcom CEO Hock Tan compared such spending to “casino gambling.” Broadcom shares slipped 0.3%.Elsewhere, Nvidia declined 0.4%, Intel fell 1.1%, AMD lost 1.2%, and Marvell Technology dropped 2.2%.Despite its recent losses, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index remains up more than 70% this year, supported by expectations of strong AI-related demand.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.content:encoded:

English football 'dangerously exposed' to financial risk, regulator finds

FAST

Oct 13 : English soccer clubs are "dangerously exposed" to financial risk, the country's Independent Football Regulator said in a report released on Tuesday, after finding that 94 per cent of clubs in the top five divisions were operating at a loss. The IFR, established last year, proposed stronger cost controls and contingency planning as part of a six-point plan to improve the financial sustainability of the English game. Its draft State of the Game report, which will undergo an eight-week public consultation before a final version is published, found nearly two-thirds of English Football League and National League clubs were "technically insolvent" and increasingly dependent on cash injections from owners. "While some of our clubs are among the richest and most competitive in the world, others are standing on the edge of financial disaster... A significant number of clubs have told us they would not survive if their owners walked away," said IFR Chair David Kogan.

The regulator said clubs should manage financial risks more effectively and have contingency plans in place should owners withdraw their support. Britain’s culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, said the findings painted a stark picture of club finances. “Football fans for years have lived with the anxiety of knowing their club could be one bad owner or poor month away from ruin," she said in a statement. "This report doesn’t just validate that anxiety, it has blown the doors off the game with the most stark uncovering of the state of football club finances in England today." PREMIER LEAGUE BACKS REPORT The Premier League said it agreed with the report's preference for a "football-led solution to revenue distribution." "As the report makes clear, new funding must go hand in hand with effective financial controls and wider reforms to strengthen clubs," the league said in a statement. The Premier League is negotiating a new revenue-sharing deal with the English Football League. Media reports said that Premier League clubs have offered to provide £1.8 billion ($2.38 billion) over 10 years, in addition to existing funding, but the EFL has asked for £1 billion over five years. "We believe the proposal we have made to the EFL, which was unanimously approved by Premier League clubs in July, meets the objectives the IFR has set out in its report," the Premier League added. NO POLITICAL PRESSURE OVER MAN CITY CASE, KOGAN SAYS Kogan said he had faced no political pressure since Manchester City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules by an independent commission. City have appealed the decision and continue to maintain their innocence, saying the commission's opinion contains "clear material errors". The IFR has the power to assess the suitability of club owners over financial wrongdoing, raising the possibility of scrutiny of City’s ownership if the club loses its appeal against the ruling. "I (have) made it very clear … any form of political interference on the way we operate is going to result in my resigning from this role," Kogan told reporters at Manchester's National Football Museum. "Just to be crystal clear, we’ve come under absolutely no political pressure whatsoever on this or any other topic." ($1 = 0.7551 pounds)

Source: Reuters

item.title: EPA proposes full reallocation of refinery biofuel exemptions
item.description: The US Environmental Protection Agency proposed on Tuesday to make larger refiners blend more biofuels into their products over the next two years, a move that will likely appeal to farm-state voters ahead of November's congressional elections.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Cavale
item.content:encoded: The US Environmental Protection Agency proposed on Tuesday to make larger refiners blend more biofuels into their products over the next two years, a move that will likely appeal to farm-state voters ahead of November's congressional elections. The proposal would help offset concerns about lost demand for ethanol producers and farmers after the EPA announced in August it would waive renewable fuel volume obligations for 29 [USN:L1N44S0OE TEXT:"small refineries"] that argued the requirements would cause economic hardship. The EPA proposed reallocating 100% of those waived fuel volume obligations and is seeking public comment after putting forward two approaches. One would split the additional 2025 small refinery exemption volume evenly between the 2026 and 2027 compliance years, while the other would allocate all of it to 2027. Comments are due by December 4, 2026, the EPA said in a statement. Renewable credit prices for biodiesel and ethanol fell slightly on the news, according to a refinery trader at the OPIS biofuels conference in Chicago. The EPA in August decided to grant [USN:L1N44S0OE TEXT:"1.76 billion RINs"] worth of small refinery exemptions for the 2025 compliance year, including full exemptions for 18 refineries and partial waivers for 11 others. At the time, the agency said it would seek to reallocate the exempted volumes to other refiners in future years to preserve overall biofuel blending requirements. The exemptions, the [USN:L1N40F0R6 TEXT:"largest ever issued"] under the Renewable Fuel Standard, drew sharp criticism from biofuel producers and farm groups, which argued they would reduce demand for ethanol and biodiesel and undermine markets for agricultural feedstocks. Refiners said compliance costs and elevated RIN prices justified relief for facilities facing economic hardship. "While we believe most of the exemptions were unjustified, EPA's reallocation plan, if finalized as proposed, will help offset the demand loss for ethanol producers and farmers," said Geoff Cooper, CEO of the Renewable Fuels Association, which represents ethanol producers. The EPA also said reallocating the waived obligations could require extending the 2026 compliance year deadline of March 31, 2027.

item.title: In Yemen's Taiz, shelling worsens and prices spiral
item.description: With their city encircled by Houthi fighters, residents of Taiz say they face intensifying bombardment and dwindling supplies as the Iran-aligned group tightens its grip on surrounding areas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: With their city encircled by Houthi fighters, residents of Taiz say they face intensifying bombardment and dwindling supplies as the Iran-aligned group tightens its grip on surrounding areas. Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, has emerged as a major theatre of the [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"conflict between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government"], after their war was reignited last month by the U.S.-Iran confrontation in the Gulf. The Houthis cut off a main road from Taiz to Aden last week, leaving [USN:L1N45S0OS TEXT:"government forces encircled."] The International Organization for Migration (IOM) said the situation in Taiz had significantly deteriorated in recent days, and that people, basic supplies and humanitarian goods could not enter the city, driving up prices. Yemen's internationally recognised government [USN:L1N45Q02D TEXT:"launched a campaign"] last week to recapture areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the [USN:L1N45S0OS TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"], a global shipping artery. But the Houthis have kept up the pressure near Taiz, seizing the town of Mudiriyat al-Misrakh some 25 km (15 miles) south of the city on Monday, military sources said. Residents reported heavy shelling of Taiz city on Monday night. Government sources said the Houthis were to blame. A spokesperson for the Houthis did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "We lived a night of terror because of the continuous bombardment," said Ahmed Mahmoud, a resident reached by phone. "This morning there is calm and worry. The streets are empty." Yassine Muqbil, another Taiz resident contacted by phone, said there had been widespread shelling and his child was too afraid to go outside. Taiz city had an estimated population of almost 600,000, Katja Juric, IOM's Aden-based Head of Programmes, told Reuters. Government sources said 80,000 had fled in the latest fighting. INCREASING PRESSURE Military sources reported fighting in al-Dabab, 10 km (6 miles) from Taiz, and on Sabar Mountain, which overlooks the city to the south, saying government forces who had withdrawn from surrounding areas had regrouped in the city. Yemeni government warplanes targeted Houthi fighters and equipment in Dabab and Misrakh, government forces said in a statement on Tuesday. For the Houthis, seizing Taiz city would be a big boost 12 years since the war first erupted. It would leave oil-rich Marib as the last city under government control in northern Yemen. Mohammed Al-Qadhi, a political and conflict analyst, said Monday evening's heavy shelling and the “tight siege” imposed by Houthi fighters indicated increasing pressure on the city. "The Houthis know the value of Taiz governorate," he said, noting that its countryside overlooks the coastline and Bab el-Mandeb and that it had served as a bastion of "resistance against the Houthis and their ideology". The Yemen war erupted in 2014 when [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"the Houthis"] seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south. Fearful of growing Iranian influence and chaos on its borders, Saudi Arabia led a military intervention against the Houthis in early 2015 to restore the government. The resulting civil war triggered one of the world's biggest humanitarian crises and led to years of fighting and devastating airstrikes by the Saudi-led coalition. The UN brokered a 2022 truce between the warring sides in Yemen that maintained peace until this year. 'CANNOT FIND FOOD' In Taiz city, prices of basic goods have shot up. "By God, we know families who cannot find their daily food," resident Nashwan Saad said on Sunday, adding that a sack of wheat had gone up by as much as some 40%. IOM's Juric said access to Taiz city had been "significantly constrained", noting that a small bottle of water now cost up to $4. "The prices of basic commodities that are still available in the city have gone up significantly," she said. "People are rushing to purchase and to stockpile basic commodities as they're anticipating a prolonged conflict and also further supply disruptions in the city." Abdulrahman al-Qulaia, director general of the Ministry of Industry and Trade Office in Taiz, cautioned against panic. "We appeal to the entire international community concerned with this matter, to humanitarian organisations and civil society organisations, to work seriously to provide these needs ... and lift the siege on the province."

item.title: ロシアのミサイル攻撃前、同盟国から警戒情報なし＝ゼレンスキー氏
item.description: [ワシントン １３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　１３日　ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１３日、ロシアによる首都キーウへの弾道ミサイル攻撃に先立ち、西側のパートナー諸国からの警戒情報がなかったと明らかにした。一方、トランプ米大統領は、ロシア製油所への攻撃停止を求めてウクライナに圧力をかけつつも、米国は引き続きウクライナと情報共有を行っていると述べた。

ゼレンスキー大統領はＸへの投稿で、トランプ氏が１１日、ロシアとウクライナが双方のエネルギー関連施設への攻撃停止で「合意した」と発表して以降、ウクライナはロシアの製油所を攻撃していないと説明。その上で、同盟国から通常得られる弾道ミサイル発射の警戒情報がないまま、夜間にキーウに対する「極めて卑劣な」攻撃が行われ、ミサイル５発が民間インフラに着弾したと述べた。

「ロシアの弾道ミサイル発射に関する情報は人命救助に役立つ。これは最も重要な問題の一つだ」としつつ、警戒情報がなかったことと米国の脅しに結び付けることは避けた。

一方、トランプ氏は１３日、米国は引き続きウクライナと情報共有を行っており、ロシアとウクライナの戦争終結を望んでいると述べた。

トランプ氏は記者団に対し「われわれはウクライナを支援しており、情報も共有している」とし、「戦争の終結を望んでいる。そのため、戦争を終わらせるためにウクライナともロシアとも協議を続けている」と語った。

ロイターなどは、米当局者がウクライナに対しロシアの製油所への攻撃を停止しなければ、情報共有や武器売却を打ち切る可能性があると警告したと報じていた。ただ、ウクライナのシビハ外相はこの日、ウクライナは米国から引き続き情報提供を受けていると述べている。

item.title: Banquero central colombiano ve tasas altas por un periodo largo y no descarta nuevas alzas
item.description: Los precios de los alimentos constituyen un riesgo clave. El Banco Central ha elevado recientemente su previsión de inflación alimentaria para este año del 9 % al 10,5 %, mientras que un fenómeno de ...
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias, Jorgelina do Rosario, Oscar Medina
item.content:encoded: Bogotá — Según un alto responsable de política monetaria, es posible que los costes de financiación en Colombia tengan que seguir subiendo y mantenerse elevados durante más tiempo para frenar los crecientes riesgos de inflación. El fenómeno meteorológico de El Niño, la guerra con Irán y un abultado déficit fiscal amenazan con avivar las presiones sobre los precios, afirmó el codirector del Banco Central, Mauricio Villamizar. “Tenemos en cuenta que los tipos se mantendrán altos durante más tiempo”, declaró Villamizar el martes en una entrevista al margen de la reunión anual del Fondo Monetario Internacional en Bangkok. “Pero también se barajan subidas adicionales si fuera necesario”. Colombia subió inesperadamente los tipos de interés el mes pasado hasta su nivel más alto desde 2024, en un intento del banco central por recuperar la credibilidad tras años sin alcanzar su objetivo de inflación. El Niño podría ejercer una mayor presión sobre los costes de los alimentos y la energía de lo que los mercados prevén actualmente, lo que situaría al país en «territorio desconocido», señaló Villamizar. Las secuelas del devastador terremoto de agosto también podrían avivar las presiones sobre los precios, añadió. Los analistas del banco central prevén que la inflación cierre el año en el 7,2 %, que se modere hasta el 4,7 % en 2027 y que alcance el objetivo del 3 % a finales de 2028, señaló Villamizar. Los precios de los alimentos constituyen un riesgo clave. El Banco Central ha elevado recientemente su previsión de inflación alimentaria para este año del 9 % al 10,5 %, mientras que un fenómeno de El Niño de gran intensidad podría elevarla hasta el 12 %, señaló Villamizar. El Gobierno del presidente Abelardo De la Espriella, que asumió el cargo en agosto, se enfrenta a un déficit presupuestario que podría superar el 9 % del producto interior bruto el próximo año. La Administración está preparando un paquete de medidas de ajuste que incluye recortes del gasto y negociaciones con los prestamistas multilaterales sobre la financiación. El país mantiene negociaciones para un nuevo programa del FMI, que el Banco Central espera que pueda anunciarse a finales de octubre. Villamizar afirmó que no conocía los detalles, pero que un acuerdo enviaría una señal positiva a los mercados. Sin embargo, para que esto allane el camino hacia una bajada de los tipos de interés, el Banco Central necesitaría comprobar que el Gobierno y el Congreso llevan a cabo los recortes fiscales. “Si se llevaran a cabo esos recortes, creo que eso aceleraría el momento en que decidamos bajar los tipos”, afirmó Villamizar. “Pero eso no significa que vayamos a bajar los tipos en cuanto consigan un programa, y mucho menos a corto plazo”. South Africa lacked fight in Australia loss, captain Bavuma says

DURBAN, Oct 13 : South Africa did not show enough fight and were let down by their mental aptitude, captain Temba Bavuma said on Tuesday after they were beaten by Australia in the first test. South Africa, who upset Australia in last year’s World Test Championship final in London, suffered a heavy 214-run defeat at Kingsmead after being bowled out for 206 in their second innings. “It’s disappointing. It's not the way you want to start a series, right? Any kind of series, let alone one against a top outfit like Australia,” Bavuma told reporters. “There are obvious things that we could definitely improve on, whether it's from the batting point of view or the bowling but yeah, it's not a happy change room.”

South Africa negated losing the toss, often crucial at the Durban venue, by having the tourists floundering on the first day but then Matt Renshaw scored 190 to steer Australia to a handy first innings total of 390 and they never looked back after that. “You have to praise the Australians the way they hung in when we had them 124-6. As a bowling attack, you're betting on yourself to restrict them to less than 250 and for them to go and get that big score, I think mentally took a little bit out of us,” added Bavuma, who saw his unbeaten record as captain ended. AUSTRALIA SET THE EXAMPLE When South Africa went out to bat, they were faced with the same favourable batting conditions. “We weren’t able to make the most of it. Australia’s lower order spent time at the crease and really showed what was possible once the ball got soft.  “In the second innings they played like a team that was in front. They put us under pressure, took command of the game, and in our second innings, there was just not enough fight and mental aptitude from us,” the captain said. Aiden Markram was the only South African batsman to score more than 50 in the match, batting for most of Tuesday as he tried to keep a rearguard fight intact before being dismissed near the end for 75. It was South Africa’s first test since their 2-0 series win in India last November and Bavuma was asked about his side being “rusty”. “I can’t sit here and use that as an excuse. You can never really prepare for test cricket without playing test cricket. But a lot of the mistakes we made out there were mental, so I think that's where we really let ourselves down," he said. “In saying that, whatever cobwebs were there, I guess are dusted out and we have another opportunity in a couple of days.” The second test is at St George’s Park in Gqeberha (formerly Port Elizabeth), starting on Sunday.

(Editing by Pritha Sarkar)

item.title: Mercados argentinos reanudan operatoria en alza, inflación en línea con lo esperado
item.description: Los negocios financieros de Argentina se reanudaron el martes con tendencia alcista entre los activos de mayor liquidez, mientras el dato de inflación de septiembre estuvo en línea a lo esperado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los negocios financieros de Argentina se reanudaron el martes con tendencia alcista entre los activos de mayor liquidez, mientras el dato de inflación de septiembre estuvo en línea a lo esperado. La actividad de mercados viene de un impás el lunes por un feriado nacional, por lo que los precios se reacomodaron a la realidad de las principales plazas externas, más una fuerte intervención cambiaria del banco central (BCRA) para frenar la apreciación de la moneda nacional. El índice de precios al consumidor ([USN:ZON00GM02 TEXT:"IPC"]) del noveno mes arrojó un 1,9%, igual al sondeo de [USN:L1N45U0LZ TEXT:"Reuters"] entre analistas y algo por arriba del 1,7% de agosto. "La data inflacionaria importa porque será la base para las tasas a pagarse desde el Gobierno en la licitación del miércoles. No se espera una sorpresa", dijo previamente un agente de Bull Market Brokers. La consultora GMA Capital Research agregó que "la clave, hacia adelante (...) sigue con señales mixtas. La actividad dio algo de aire en agosto sin despejar el riesgo de una nueva recesión técnica en el tercer trimestre", afirmó. El índice accionario S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa porteña subió un 1,45% al cierre y los bonos soberanos extrabursátiles promediaron una ganancia del 0,3%, junto a un riesgo país firme en los 596 puntos básicos (2000 GMT). "El riesgo país bajó en la semana pasada, impulsado por el mejor clima regional tras las elecciones en Brasil, aunque las tasas globales siguen elevadas y los fundamentos locales aún muestran señales mixtas", resaltó el agente de liquidación y compensación Cohen. "En este contexto, los bonos recuperaron algo de terreno, pero el margen para una mejora sostenida sigue condicionado por el escenario externo y la evolución doméstica", acotó. En un clima de tranquilidad, el peso mayorista avanzó un 0,2% a 1.514 por dólar , el nivel más alto en casi un mes, en momentos en que el BCRA busca sumar divisas a diario para respaldar sus reservas internacionales. La autoridad monetaria compró 291 millones de dólares en el inicio de una semana corta, y así superó los 15.000 millones en el transcurso del 2026. Con la idea de cubrir vencimientos de deuda interna a corto plazo, el Tesoro argentino realizará el miércoles su primera licitación mensual, una movida habitual debido a que tiene cerrada la posibilidad de financiamiento externo por los altos costos a pagar. El Fondo Monetario Internacional ([USN:L6N45Y115 TEXT:"FMI"]) recortó el crecimiento de Argentina en 2026 hasta el 2,1%, desde el 3,5% de julio, el ajuste más profundo entre las principales economías de la región, y elevó su previsión de inflación al 32,5%. "La combinación de menor actividad y precios rígidos da a las perspectivas un tinte estanflacionario. Es probable que el mercado lo interprete (a la retracción del PIB) como una confirmación más que como una sorpresa", sostuvo Ion Jauregui, analista de ActivTrades. La [USN:L6N45Y0SY TEXT:"economía argentina"] se recuperará lentamente a medida que el país se acerca a un año electoral en 2027, tras haber entrado probablemente en recesión en el tercer trimestre, según una encuesta de analistas realizada por Reuters. El ministro de Economía de Argentina, Luis Caputo, dijo en su cuenta en X que mantuvo en Tailandia una "excelente reunión" con las autoridades del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI), donde se analizaron "todos los temas, internos y externos". La titular del organismo, Kristalina Georgieva, "fue muy elogiosa en particular de la disciplina fiscal (de Argentina), a la que calificó como ejemplar en el mundo, a pesar de los shocks globales. Los equipos (técnicos) seguirán trabajando para finalizar la tercera revisión", agregó el funcionario, recientemente ratificado en su cargo por el presidente Milei. Argentina y el FMI tienen un acuerdo vigente por 20.000 millones de dólares y, con la esperada aprobación de la nueva revisión, el país debería recibir unos 860 millones de dólares.

item.title: 米債利回りに上昇余地、ＦＲＢあと1─2回利上げも＝ＰＩＭＣＯのＣＩＯ
item.description:
Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
[ニューヨーク １３日 ロイター] - 世界最大の債券運用会社ＰＩ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米債利回りに上昇余地、ＦＲＢあと1─2回利上げも＝ＰＩＭＣＯのＣＩＯ 1:12 配信

Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss

[ニューヨーク １３日 ロイター] - 世界最大の債券運用会社ＰＩＭＣＯの最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）、ダニエル・アイバシン氏は１３日、米国債利回りには一段の上昇余地があるとの見方を示した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は現在の金融引き締めサイクルを終える前にあと１回か２回の利上げに踏み切る可能性が高いという。

アイバシン氏はグランツ秋季会議の合間に取材に応じ、ＦＲＢが今月下旬の会合では金利を据え置くと予想する一方、追加で１─２回の利上げの余地があるとの見方を提示。「ＦＲＢはひとまず金利を据え置き、２０２６年中におそらくもう１回利上げするだろう。現在の見通しを踏まえると、われわれはあと１─２回の引き締めを予想している」と述べた。

item.title: Nvidia buys stakes in French tech startups Doctolib, Genesis AI
item.description: US chipmaker Nvidia has agreed to buy stakes in French technology startups Doctolib and Genesis AI, the two French companies said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA.O) has agreed to buy stakes in French technology startups Doctolib and Genesis AI, the two French companies said on Tuesday. Doctolib said that Nvidia had agreed to buy a minority stake without specifying the size of the stake or its value, though it said the presence of Nvidia would help it to develop artificial intelligence tools. Genesis AI confirmed an earlier report from Les Echos newspaper. "We are excited that Nvidia is a strategic investor in Genesis AI," it said in a statement. The newspaper added the chip maker bought stakes in Entalpic and Pigment. The two companies did not respond immediately to requests for comment.

PARIS, Oct 13 : France's cybersecurity agency said on Tuesday that the refrigeration systems of Copeland and Dixell were also hacked during a cyberattack that targeted supermarket refrigerators and freezers. A spokesperson for Copeland, which owns Dixell, declined to confirm the information and said the company's top priority is to protect customers' operations. Hackers raised temperatures of refrigerators in hundreds of supermarkets to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit), causing fires and spoiling food.

Oct 13 : Alphabet's Google on Wednesday released its flagship AI model Gemini 4 Argon to developers and businesses worldwide, seeking to regain ground against rivals OpenAI and Anthropic after months of delays and a leadership shakeup at its DeepMind lab.  The model excels at "deep work" on complex, multi-step tasks in coding, finance, law, cybersecurity and science, Google said. API pricing at launch starts at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with rates set to double after November 30.  The release follows a rocky stretch in Google's AI efforts. The company announced in September that it no longer planned to release Gemini 3.5 Pro, which CEO Sundar Pichai had originally said would be released in June. It also overhauled DeepMind after the AI lab's co-founder and CEO Demis Hassabis stepped aside and several leaders of its Gemini model left the company.

Argon is available to paying customers through the company's AI application building tools. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can access it through the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, while the Antigravity coding tool is limited to Ultra subscribers. Teams using Argon in Antigravity increased agentic code submissions by more than 35 per cent, while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third, Google said.   Customers testing the model early include Deloitte, LexisNexis, Ambience Healthcare and Isomorphic Labs. Meanwhile, Google said it would open its Fairwind Program to hundreds of additional partners. The program gives vetted cybersecurity defenders a version of Argon without its cyber guardrails. In September, the company had said it was providing the model to select cybersecurity partners. Separately, Google will offer 10,000 scientists six months of free access to Antigravity's highest usage tier.

Source: Reuters

item.title: ＯＰＥＣプラス産油量、9月は日量90万バレル増 サウジが出荷拡大
item.description:
Alex Lawler Olesya Astakhova
[ロンドン １３日] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Alex Lawler　Olesya Astakhova

[ロンドン　１３日] - 石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）が１３日公表した月報によると、ＯＰＥＣ加盟国とロシアなど非加盟産油国で構成する「ＯＰＥＣプラス」の９月の産油量は日量平均３９０７万バレルで、８月から日量約９０万バレル増えた。ホルムズ海峡の混乱が続く中でも、サウジアラビアからの出荷が拡大した。ただ、今年２月末のイラン交戦開始前の水準は依然として下回っている。

湾岸地域からの供給は、ここ数週間回復傾向が見られる。サウジの９月の産油量は日量８３７万２０００バレルと、８月より２００万バレル超増えた。東西パイプラインへの攻撃で紅海経由の出荷が一時混乱した後、国有石油会社サウジアラムコが湾岸の輸出ターミナルからの積み出しを拡大した。一方、ウクライナによる製油所などへの攻撃を受けるロシアの生産量は日量３万８０００バレル減った。

ＯＰＥＣは、２０２６年の世界石油需要の見通しを日量１８万バレル増に引き下げた。６カ月連続の下方修正。一方、２７年は石油備蓄の放出分を補充する必要があるとして、前年比日量２５５万バレル増の日量平均１億８３０万バレルと予測した。

item.title: US Senate report says spending on consultants for internet subsidy program tops $200 million annually
item.description: A US Senate committee report released on Tuesday said consultants who assist schools and libraries in winning funding from a $3 billion annual internet subsidy program receive between $200 million and $400 million annually.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: A US Senate committee report released on Tuesday said consultants who assist schools and libraries in winning funding from a $3 billion annual internet subsidy program receive between $200 million and $400 million annually. Senate Commerce Committee chair Ted Cruz said consultants help the applicants for the Federal Communications Commission E-Rate program "comply with a Byzantine process that has become a costly feature of the program." He added that the high fees should "prompt greater scrutiny of how E-Rate funds move, who benefits and whether the program's current structure delivers value to schools, libraries and taxpayers." The FCC has been subsidizing connectivity to and within schools for almost 30 years. The report found that some consultants charge school districts $100,000 or more per year. Milwaukee Public Schools has participated in E-Rate for more than two decades and has received more than $115 million in funding but is still paying more than $250,000 annually in consulting services, the report said. "The continued need for significant consultant support raises questions about the extent to which long-term participants remain dependent on outside expertise to navigate the program," the report said. The school district and the FCC did not immediately comment. The report added that the consultants are subject to limited oversight and cited a number of criminal cases in E-Rate fraud cases and recommended the FCC require public disclosure of consultant compensation associated with E-Rate and urged the commission to stop expansion of E-Rate until its vulnerabilities are addressed. In June, FCC Chair Brendan Carr said the commission was launching a comprehensive review of the E-Rate program, adding that it could reform the scheme or end it. The FCC is reviewing whether the program has fulfilled its mission and whether continued funding is consistent with Congress' objective. E-Rate is funded by fees paid by telecom companies that are collected from consumers through the "Universal Service Fee" on monthly phone bills.
